newsitem.title: UK: Iraq fears hike oil, FTSE closes at record.
newsitem.headline: Iraq fears hike oil, FTSE closes at record.

text.p: Talk of possible U.S. attacks on Iraq pushed world oil prices to post Gulf War peaks on Thursday, while London's blue chip FTSE stock index closed at a record high on the back of a strong Wall Street.
On the foreign exchanges, the dollar staged a late revival against the mark on German rate comments and also firmed on the yen.
Leading European shares closed higher after U.S. prices data eased inflation fears and the Dow Average jumped through its record closing high of 5,778.00 set in mid-May.

London's FTSE 100 index ended at a new peak of 3932.6 -- 13.9 points above its previous closing high on August 28 -- helped by the bullish Dow and a clutch of leading British company results which beat expectations.
Talk of possible attacks on Iraq by the United States and confirmation that stealth bombers were heading for the Gulf pushed oil prices higher.

At one point the October Brent contract, which expires on Friday, had gained 81 cents to $24.39 a barrel -- its highest level since January 1991 after Iraq invaded Kuwait in 1990 and pushed Brent prices to $40.95.
By 1600 GMT Brent had fallen back sharply from the day's highs to around $23.75 as traders took profits from the week's $2 hike in prices, but it was well above Wednesday's close.
Prices peaked on market fears that Baghdad might mount an assault against Kuwait after the Kuwaitis agreed to serve as a base for an expected U.S. military strike on Iraq.
On the foreign exchange front, the dollar managed to claw its way back above 1.51 marks in afternoon trading but lacked the incentive to reclaim the near-two month high of 1.5155 hit on Wednesday.
It firmed on the mark after a Bundesbank council member said he saw more room for Germany to cut key interest rates.
Klaus-Dieter Kuehbacher, president of the regional central bank of Berlin and Brandenburg, said rates, including the 2.50-percent discount rate, could fall more if economic conditions permitted.
In Frankfurt German shares ended a lively post-bourse session just one point off their record high, boosted calming U.S. inflation fears, firm German debt and the strong dollar.
Dealers were bullish, saying the market could break records on Friday.
Wall Street's strength also boosted French stocks which finished sharply up, with a shove from bank stocks after strong first-half results and a healthy oil share performance.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index ended 27.31 points or 1.34 percent up at 2,065.37.
CURRENCIES AT 1600 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5130 marks and 110.20 yen compared with late Wednesday's 1.5079 marks and 110.20 yen.
STOCK MARKETS - CLOSING INDICES
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares ended 27.2 points higher at 3,932.8.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished up 27.31 at 2,065.37.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 3.52 at 2,570.32. In post-bourse trade the IBIS-DAX index rose to 2,588.04.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed weaker in Europe at $381.90, down 60 cents. Silver finished at $5.02, down seven cents.
